The probability that both the first and the second balls are red is (1/3)(3/5)(2/4) + (2/3)(1/4)(0/3) = 1/10. The required conditional probability is (1/10)/(11/30) = 3/11. The posterior probability that the box is A, 6/11, is the trap.

items.question: In how many ways can 7 people be seated in a row so that two particular people, A and B, are NOT together, and a third particular person, C, sits at one of the ends?
items.explanation: C can sit at either end, giving 2 choices. The remaining 6 people must be arranged with A and B not together: 6! minus 2 x 5! = 720 minus 240 = 480 ways. The total is 2 x 480 = 960. Forgetting the end condition gives 3600.

items.question: In a school, 120 students offered Hindi, 70 French and 75 Sanskrit. Of these, 58 offered Hindi only, 41 French only, 12 Hindi and French only, and 9 French and Sanskrit only. How many students are there in total?
items.explanation: Work through the Venn regions in order. The French total gives the all-three region as 70 minus 41 minus 12 minus 9, which is 8. The Hindi total then gives the Hindi-and-Sanskrit-only region as 42, and the Sanskrit total gives the Sanskrit-only region as 16. Adding all seven regions gives 186. Adding the three subject totals, or forgetting the all-three region, gives the other options.

items.question: If x = sqrt(7 + 2 sqrt(6)) + sqrt(7 - 2 sqrt(6)), what is the value of x^2 + 1/x^2?
items.explanation: Squaring gives x^2 = 7 + 2 sqrt(6) + 7 - 2 sqrt(6) + 2 sqrt(49 - 24) = 14 + 10 = 24. Then x^2 + 1/x^2 = 24 + 1/24 = 577/24. Subtracting the reciprocal instead of adding gives 575/24.

items.question: If sin A + cos A = 5/4, what is the value of sin^3 A + cos^3 A?
items.explanation: Squaring gives sin^2 A + cos^2 A + 2 sin A cos A = 25/16, so sin A cos A = 9/32. Then sin^3 A + cos^3 A = (sin A + cos A)^3 - 3 sin A cos A (sin A + cos A) = 125/64 - 135/128 = 115/128.

items.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground is 30 degrees. After moving 40 m towards the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 60 degrees. What is the distance from the second position to the top of the tower?
items.explanation: Let the height be h. From the first point, the distance to the base is h divided by tan 30, and from the second point it is h divided by tan 60. The difference is 40 m, so h times (the square root of 3 minus 1 over the square root of 3) = 40, giving h = 20 times the square root of 3 m. The slant distance from the second point is the square root of h squared plus (h over the square root of 3) squared, which is 2h over the square root of 3 = 40 m. The height itself, 20 times the square root of 3 m, is the trap.

items.question: What is the value of x? Statement I: x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0. Statement II: x is even.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives x equal to 3 or 4, so it leaves two possibilities and is not sufficient. Statement II alone only says x is even, which does not fix its value. Together, the even root is 4, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: Is X the grandmother of Y? Statement I: X is the mother of Z. Statement II: Z is the father of Y.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives only that X is Z's mother, and statement II gives only that Z is Y's father. Together they make X the mother of Y's father, which is the definition of a grandmother, so both statements together are sufficient. Either statement alone leaves the chain open.

items.question: What is the area of a circle? The radius of the circle is a whole number of centimetres. Statement I: The area is between 100 and 200 square cm. Statement II: The circumference is between 42 and 51 cm.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone allows the radius to be 6 or 7 cm, since the squares 36 and 49 times pi fall in the range, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone allows the radius to be 7 or 8 cm, since 2 pi times 7 is about 44 and 2 pi times 8 is about 50.3, so it is not sufficient. Together the radius must be 7 cm, giving an area of 154 square cm, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What is the present age of A? Statement I: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 2 : 3. Statement II: Five years ago, the ratio of their ages was 1 : 2.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives only the ratio, and statement II gives only a past ratio. Together they fix the ages: if A is 2k and B is 3k, then (2k - 5) / (3k - 5) is 1/2, giving k equal to 5, so A is 10. Each statement alone leaves the scale unknown.

items.question: A faulty clock was set right on Friday night. What time will it show at 10 AM on Sunday? Statement I: The clock loses 3 minutes every hour. Statement II: It was set right at 10 PM on Friday.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: From 10 PM on Friday to 10 AM on Sunday is 36 hours. The clock loses 3 minutes an hour, so it loses 36 x 3 = 108 minutes, which is 1 hour 48 minutes, and it therefore shows 10 AM minus 1 hour 48 minutes, which is 8:12 AM. Statement I alone gives the rate but not the starting time, and Statement II alone gives the starting time but not the rate, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What day of the week was 26 January 2026? Statement I: 1 March 2026 was a Sunday. Statement II: February 2026 had 28 days.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone does not fix the day, because the number of days in February is unknown: if February had 29 days, 26 January would fall on a different day. Statement II alone says nothing about any day of the week. Together, February has 28 days, so 1 February was also a Sunday, and 26 January, six days earlier, was a Monday, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: How many students play only cricket? Statement I: 80 students play cricket and 50 play football. Statement II: 30 students play both games and there are 120 students in all.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives the cricket total but not the overlap, and statement II alone gives the overlap but not the cricket total. Together, the number playing only cricket is 80 minus 30, which is 50. Both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What is the area of a rectangle? The length and breadth of the rectangle are whole numbers of centimetres. Statement I: The length of the rectangle is twice its breadth. Statement II: The perimeter of the rectangle is between 35 cm and 37 cm.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone leaves the breadth free, so the area is not fixed. Statement II alone gives a perimeter between 35 cm and 37 cm, and with whole-number sides the perimeter must be 36 cm, so length plus breadth is 18 cm, but many pairs give that sum and the area varies. Together, length is twice breadth and length plus breadth is 18 cm, so breadth is 6 cm, length is 12 cm and the area is 72 square cm, a unique answer. Both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: Is y divisible by 12? Statement I: y is divisible by 3. Statement II: y is divisible by 4.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Divisibility by 3 alone does not guarantee divisibility by 12, and divisibility by 4 alone does not either. Together they do, since 3 and 4 are coprime and their product is 12. So both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: Is n divisible by 6? Statement I: n is divisible by 2. Statement II: n squared is divisible by 9.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives divisibility by 2 only, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone gives divisibility by 3, since if 9 divides n squared then 3 divides n, but it says nothing about divisibility by 2, so it is not sufficient. Together, n is divisible by both 2 and 3, so it is divisible by 6, and both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What is the distance covered by a car? Statement I: The car covers the first stretch of its journey at 60 km per hour for 2 hours. Statement II: The car covers the second stretch at 90 km per hour for 1 hour.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives only the first stretch, 120 km, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone gives only the second stretch, 90 km, so it is not sufficient. Together, the distance is 120 + 90 = 210 km, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What is the profit percentage on the cost price? Statement I: The marked price is 25% above the cost price. Statement II: The article is sold at a discount of 20% on the marked price.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives the marked price as 1.25 times the cost price but no selling price, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone gives the selling price as 0.80 times the marked price but no cost price, so it is not sufficient. Together, the selling price is 0.80 x 1.25 = 1.00 times the cost price, so the profit is 0%, and both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What is the average age of a class of 40 students? Statement I: The average age of 20 boys in the class is 22 years. Statement II: The average age of 20 girls in the class is 18 years.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives only the boys' total age, 440 years, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone gives only the girls' total age, 360 years, so it is not sufficient. Together, the average is (440 + 360)/40 = 20 years, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What is the value of x + y? Statement I: x = 2y. Statement II: x - y = 6.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives only the ratio of x to y, and statement II gives only their difference. Together they fix x as 12 and y as 6, so x + y is 18, and both statements together are sufficient. Each statement alone leaves the pair unfixed, which is the missing-piece pattern.

items.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle? Statement I: The length of the rectangle is 12 cm. Statement II: The diagonal of the rectangle is 13 cm.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives only the length, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone gives only the diagonal, so it is not sufficient. Together, the breadth is the square root of 13 squared minus 12 squared, which is 5 cm, so the perimeter is 2 x (12 + 5) = 34 cm, and both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: If the figure for VoltAuto rises by 25% and the figure for GreenDrive falls by 25%, what is their new combined total?

diagram.caption: Electric vehicles sold by five brands in 2025 (in thousands)

items.explanation: The revised VoltAuto figure is 60 and the revised GreenDrive figure is 27, so their combined total is 87. Adding the original figures, or revising only one of them, gives the other options.

items.question: The figure for Eco Motors is 90% of its target. If the target is then raised by 20%, what is the new target?
items.explanation: The figure is 54, which is 90% of the target, so the target is 54 x 100 / 90 = 60. Raising it by 20% gives 60 x 1.20 = 72. Taking the old target, or using the figure itself, gives the other options.

items.question: For VoltAuto and GreenDrive, the given figures are the numbers that succeeded, at success rates of 96% and 72% respectively. If 10% of all attempts for the two together ended in a draw, how many attempts ended in defeat for the two together?
items.explanation: Invert each success rate: VoltAuto needed 48 x 100 / 96, which is 50 attempts, and GreenDrive needed 50 attempts, giving 100 in all. 10% of these, which is 10, ended in a draw, and 84 were successes, so the defeats are 100 minus 10 minus 84, which is 6. Forgetting the draws, or applying the draw rate to the successes, gives the other options.

items.question: How many more units must Swift EV add to equal the average of all 5 categories?
items.explanation: The average of the 5 categories is 208 divided by 5, which is 41.6. The smallest, Swift EV at 28, needs 13.6 more to reach it. Answering with the average itself, or with the gap to the largest category, gives the other options.

items.question: If the total of the first 3 categories falls by 50% and the total of the remaining categories rises by 10%, what is the ratio of the revised first total to the revised second total?
items.explanation: The first total is 138, which falls by 50% to 69, and the second total is 70, which rises by 10% to 77. The ratio of 69 to 77 simplifies to 69 : 77. Using the original totals, or reversing the ratio, gives the other options.

items.question: If every figure in August rises by 10% and the largest figure is then halved, what is the new total for that month?

diagram.caption: Rainfall in four cities, June to August (in mm)

items.explanation: The August total is 1100, so a 10% rise makes it 1210. The largest figure is 480, which rises to 528 and is then halved to 264, a fall of 264, so the new total is 1210 - 264 = 946. Applying only the 10% rise, or halving the wrong figure, gives the other options.

items.question: The Mumbai figure in August is 80% of its target. If the target is shared equally between Mumbai and Delhi, what is Delhi's share?
items.explanation: The Mumbai figure is 480, which is 80% of the target, so the target is 480 x 100 / 80 = 600. Shared equally between Mumbai and Delhi, each gets 300. Taking the target itself, or using the figure, gives the other options.

items.question: In August, Mumbai achieved 80% of its target and Delhi achieved 80% of its target. If 10% of their combined target is held in reserve, how much of the combined target remains available?
items.explanation: Invert each achievement rate: Mumbai targeted 480 x 100 / 80, which is 600, and Delhi targeted 200, giving a combined target of 800. Holding 10% in reserve leaves 90% of 800, which is 720. Answering with the combined target, or with the achieved figures, gives the other options.

items.question: If the Delhi figure is halved, which city's share of the August total exceeds one-third?
items.explanation: Halving Delhi changes the August total from 1100 to 1020, since Delhi is 160. The shares become Mumbai 480/1020 = 47.1%, Kolkata 310/1020 = 30.4%, Chennai 150/1020 = 14.7% and Delhi 80/1020 = 7.8%. Only Mumbai exceeds one-third. Using the original total, or the wrong city, gives the other options.

items.question: If the August figures for Mumbai and Chennai rise by 10% and the other figures fall by 10%, by what percentage does the August total change?
items.explanation: The rising departments gain 63 and the falling departments lose 47, so the total moves by 16 on 1100, which is 1.5%. Applying the rise to the whole total, or ignoring the fall, gives the other options.

items.question: In which year did the value show its highest percentage growth over the previous year, and what was that percentage?

diagram.caption: Tourists visiting a national park (in lakh), 2019 to 2023

items.explanation: The growth rates are 2020: -25%, 2021: +66.7%, 2022: +20% and 2023: +16.7%. The highest percentage growth was in 2021, at 66.7%. Using the largest absolute rise, or the wrong year, gives the other options.

items.question: What is the ratio of the average of the first three years to the average of the last two years?
items.explanation: The first three years average 12 and the last two average 19.5, so the ratio is 8 : 13. Reversing the ratio, or comparing totals instead of averages, gives the other options.

items.question: The chart figures are not all exact. Some years' figures are understated, each by exactly 10% below its true value, and the rest are exact. The true total over the five years is 78 lakh. Which of the following must be true?
options: At least one of the 2019 and 2020 figures is understated.
Both the 2019 and 2021 figures are understated.
items.explanation: The chart total is 75 lakh, so the understated figures fall short of their true values by 3 lakh in all. A figure understated by 10% falls short of its true value by one-ninth of the chart figure, so the chart figures of the understated years must add to 27. Only two pairs do: 2019 and 2021 (12 + 15) and 2020 and 2022 (9 + 18). Both pairs contain 2019 or 2020, so at least one of those two years must be understated. The 2023 figure is understated in neither pair; 2021 and 2022 each appear in only one pair, so neither must be understated; and the 2019 and 2021 pair is only one of the two possibilities.

items.question: By what percentage is the highest value more than the lowest value, after the lowest value is revised up by 15%?
items.explanation: The lowest value becomes 10.3 after the 15% revision, and the highest is 21, so the gap is 102.9% of the revised lowest value. Ignoring the revision, or using the highest value as the base, gives the other options.

items.question: The average of the four year-on-year percentage changes is one way to describe the growth of tourist numbers between 2019 and 2023. The compound annual growth rate over the same period is another. Which of the following is true?
options: The average of the four year-on-year percentage changes is greater than the compound annual growth rate over the same period.
The compound annual growth rate exceeds 20%.
The average of the four year-on-year percentage changes is less than 15%.
The compound annual growth rate equals the average yearly absolute change divided by the 2019 figure.
The average of the four year-on-year percentage changes equals 15%.
items.explanation: The year-on-year changes are -25% in 2020, +66.7% in 2021, +20% in 2022 and +16.7% in 2023, and their average is about 19.6%. The number rose from 12 to 21 over four years, so the compound annual growth rate is the fourth root of 21/12 minus 1, about 15.0%. The average of the yearly percentage changes is therefore greater than the compound rate. The compound rate is below 20%, the average is above 15%, and the average yearly absolute change divided by the 2019 figure is 2.25/12, or 18.75%, which is not the compound rate.
